title: Dynamics of localized solutions in three core coupled waveguides with quasi-periodic nonlinearity
authors: Bruno M. Miranda, Ardiley T. Avelar, Wesley B. Cardoso, Dionisio Bazeia
abstract: In this paper we investigate the behavior of localized solutions, specifically solitons, in a system of three coupled waveguides. The nonlinearity is modeled by a quasi-periodic modulation influencing the interaction between the waveguides. We analyze the evolution of the soliton profiles and their dynamics under varying modulation parameters, highlighting distinct behaviors such as attraction and repulsion among solitons. Our findings reveal that the system exhibits complex behaviors, depending on the interplay between the quasi-periodic modulation and the waveguide parameters. The study contributes to understanding the impact of quasi-periodic nonlinearity on soliton dynamics in coupled waveguide systems, laying the groundwork for potential applications in nonlinear optics and photonic devices.
summary: This work analyzes how quasi-periodic nonlinear modulation affects the dynamics of solitons in three coupled optical waveguides. By simulating the system, the authors demonstrate that the sign of the modulation dictates whether solitons experience attraction, leading to bound states, or repulsion, causing them to separate. This research is significant for understanding and controlling light pulse propagation in advanced nonlinear optical devices.
main_problem: The paper investigates the complex dynamics of localized solutions, specifically solitons, propagating in a system of three coupled waveguides.
main_result: The interaction between solitons is highly dependent on the sign of the quasi-periodic modulation amplitude ($A_0$), leading to distinct regimes of attraction (bound states) or repulsion (separation).
method: The study relies on theoretical analysis complemented by detailed numerical simulations, utilizing techniques like the split-step method and FFT.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by coupled Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations (NLS) describing three coupled optical waveguides. The coupling is modulated quasi-periodically via the cross-phase modulation coefficient, $\delta(z)$.
key_observables: Soliton profiles ($|\psi_i|^2$), center of mass, and variance of the field amplitudes.
important_parameters: The quasi-periodic modulation amplitude ($A_0$), the constant background coupling ($\delta_0$), and the wave numbers ($k_l$) defining the modulation.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system can be effectively described by the coupled NLS equations and focuses on the impact of the quasi-periodic modulation term.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spatial evolution of the field intensity for different modulation amplitudes ($A_0$), comparing stable/unstable solutions and showing the separation or convergence of solitons.
paper_structure: The paper details the model (Section II), presents numerical results analyzing different interaction regimes (Section III), and concludes with a discussion of the findings and future work (Section IV).
why_interesting: The study provides a concrete example of how time- or space-dependent nonlinear coupling terms (quasi-periodicity) can fundamentally alter the stability and interaction dynamics of nonlinear waves, which is relevant to engineered photonic systems.
